correctness.summary: The arbitrary-d Laurent coefficient fixes the only possible transition at d=(2 h_n^2+2n-1)/4. Below it, the source paper's largest-branch boundary geometry and minimum principle give the Pick property; at equality the Pick property passes by locally uniform closure; above it the positive Laurent coefficient forces eventual decrease on the positive axis.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The direct 2026 source gives an exact all-d threshold for nonlargest zeros but explicitly gives only a sufficient largest-zero interval and states that its endpoint is not claimed optimal. Searches found no prior exact largest-zero complete-Bernstein threshold. Older first-derivative monotonicity papers remain a residual literature risk because not all full texts were independently inspected.

value.summary: The result closes the sole nonsharp case in the source paper's square-root-scale phase diagram, replaces a sufficient endpoint asymptotic to n/2 by the exact Hermite-edge threshold asymptotic to 3n/2, and identifies the edge Hermite zero as the governing quantity.

limitations: Only constant-shift square-root scales sqrt(lambda+d) are classified.
No arbitrary scale-function classification is claimed.
No finite-order derivative optimization outside the complete-monotonicity regime is claimed.
The originality assessment is literature-based and older monotonicity papers were not all fully inspected.
